title: Anchor-Watch Drag Alarm
dataSources: NMEA/SignalK data (`nmea:reading`), bilge pump (`bilge:event`), mooring/anchor watch (`mooring:status`), marine weather (`marineweather:forecast`).
app: Marine electronics — NMEA 2000 / SignalK boat networks, bilge, battery and shore-power sensors, anchor-watch GPS, and marine weather feeds — streamed to Splunk HEC via SignalK and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=mooring:status event=anchor
| eval drift_m=round(sqrt(pow(lat_m-set_lat_m,2)+pow(lon_m-set_lon_m,2)),1)
| where drift_m>swing_radius_m
| sort - _time
| table _time drift_m swing_radius_m
description: Raises an alarm when the boat drifts beyond its anchor swing circle, warning that the anchor is dragging.
value: A dragging anchor overnight can put a boat on the rocks; a drift alarm buys crucial time to react.
implementation: Ingest GPS anchor-watch data into `index=personal`; alert when drift exceeds the swing radius.
visualization: Map of anchor position versus swing circle with drift alerts.
grandmaExplanation: It sounds the alarm if the boat drifts too far from where you anchored, warning the anchor is slipping.
